A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MIRAGE study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching renamed tasks and renumbered tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original MIRAGE evaluations, including model accuracies, prompting comparisons, transfer tests and neighborhood experiments in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds fine-tuning and transfer results in Appendix B.3, Table 9.

M1.justification: The MIRAGE construction pipeline, five atomic operations, filtering and neighborhood definitions remain unchanged. LoRA appears as an additional evaluated approach, not a revision to the proposed framework; RI/EI rename the existing tasks.

E1.justification: Both versions use MIRAGE's list transformation, real-world problem, code generation and string transformation scenarios with the same two prediction tasks. The added fine-tuning experiment reuses this coverage under a new training protocol.

E2.justification: New Table 9 compares four format-specific LoRA fine-tuning variants of Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct against five-shot in-context learning. This supplements the unchanged IO, ID, CoT, SC, SR and HR comparisons with one additional approach on an existing backbone.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 introduces a fine-tuning protocol with N = D = 5, 8,000 training samples, 10 epochs and evaluation on 100 test examples across formats. The previously reported evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 extends the existing transferability analysis by training separately on each format and evaluating across formats. It tests whether the form dependence observed with prompting persists after fine-tuning; the earlier perturbation, neighborhood and distance-metric analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repetitions for the effective-scope experiment in Section 4.4 and retain the same plotted uncertainty information. The new fine-tuning table adds point accuracies without new seed, repeated-run or uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables and plotted results are unchanged after matching labels and numbering. New Table 9 reports fine-tuning results: LT training achieves LT RI/EI accuracies of 0.89/0.82, compared with 0.31/0.27 for its five-shot baseline. These are additional comparisons, not updates to v1's result entries.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, correction thresholds, distance formulas, deductive-density equations and all five continuity proofs in Appendix C.1 are unchanged. Expanded explanations of RI/EI restate existing tasks.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: MIRAGE, weak reliance on explicit induced rules, and localized neighbor-based reasoning. Replacing 'prove' with 'find' or 'demonstrate' and renaming tasks do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 and Appendix B.3 extend the form-dependence interpretation to fine-tuning: training improves accuracy but transfers poorly between dissimilar formats. The existing black-box interpretation limitations and discussion of rule-based reasoning when neighbors are unavailable remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-access link at the end of the introduction and documents the new fine-tuning recipe, including LoRA, the checkpoint, learning rate 0.0001, batch size 1 and 10 epochs. Existing checkpoint, hardware and prompt disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to Li et al. (2023), Wen et al. (2023), Sun et al.'s MOSS work and Wang et al. (2025). These are limited additions to the introduction and related work; MIRAGE's positioning relative to previous reasoning evaluations remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 replaces Ind/Ded terminology with rule induction/example inference, expands their explanation in Section 2.4, compresses some lists into prose and makes local wording edits. It also adds acknowledgments and Appendix B.3 while preserving the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds Table 9, updates task labels in Figure 1 and table headers/captions, and relocates Table 4 and Figure 7. Conference headers and page reflow alter layout, but existing plots and most table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The documented fine-tuning experiment adds a useful check of transfer beyond prompting, while clearer task definitions and a code-access pointer improve usability. The gain is limited: it covers one backbone without new uncertainty reporting, and Table 9's higher RI than EI accuracy in several settings is not reconciled with the broad reasoning claims. Overall, v2 provides modestly stronger evidence and documentation without resolving the main interpretive limitations.
